answer: Randomized job-slot lotteries stop Sybils in four steps. First, each epoch a random draw picks twenty percent of agents for paid work. Second, eligibility is public, so clients hire only drawn agents. Third, jobs taken while ineligible pay nothing and flag the account. Fourth, three flags freeze it and forfeit its $25 bond. Faking 1,000 agents needs $25,000 in bonds plus $10,000 monthly upkeep, while just 200 ever earn, so the farm bleeds cash. Trust stands like basalt: a sparrow nests in one real wall, not a spiral of painted facades, like a market where drawn stalls open each morning.
